The hard part is not target identity: it is carrying with the correct gripper sign and releasing deep enough inside the plate footprint for the On predicate.\n\n## Winning technique\nIdentify the wine bottle globally as the tall dark green bottle with cork, and the destination as the white ceramic plate with red rings rather than the nearby stove burner. Back-project several agentview_high pixels on each; use wrist only to confirm the same bottle candidate before grasping.\n\nMove above the bottle at kitchen carry height, run `pi0_pick` with the short prompt `pick up the wine bottle`, and verify the grasp from gripper opening plus the wrist/agentview images. Lock with `set_gripper +1`, carry to a point over the perceived plate center, and descend to a low kitchen release pose while holding `gripper:+1`. If the first release leaves the bottle on the near plate edge and does not terminate, re-close and make a very small closed-gripper nudge deeper toward the plate center before releasing again.\n\n## Magic numbers\n`pre_pos_z=1.15` for approach above the upright bottle (band 1.13-1.17).\n`pi0_pick max_chunks=20` (band 15-22), `lift_thresh=0.05`, `gripper_closed_thresh=0.06`.\n`set_gripper +1` for 8 steps after the pick (band 5-10).\n`carry_z=1.12` (band 1.10-1.15) with `step_clip=0.015` for the loaded carry.\n`release/seat eef_z=1.02-1.03` over the plate with `step_clip=0.01` or lower.\nIf edge release does not terminate, use a closed-gripper contact nudge of about 2-3 cm in xy at the same z with `step_clip=0.006` (band 0.005-0.008), then release.\nNEVER omit `gripper:1` during carry or lowering; `move_to` defaults open if unspecified.\nNEVER classify the gray stove burner as the plate; use RGB semantics before placing.\n\n## Failure modes\n| symptom | root cause (A<N>) | fix |\n| first release leaves `terminated:false` while bottle is visibly on the near/front plate area | A1: bottle footprint was edge-biased after low release at the perceived plate center; the held bottle hung forward of the eef | re-close, make a short closed-gripper nudge deeper toward plate center at eef z about 1.03, then release again |\n\n## Re-localization per scene\nWine bottle: look for the tall dark green cylindrical bottle with a cork/gold top. Agentview_high is sufficient for identity; sample body/top pixels away from silhouette edges and median xy. The wrist view from above the agentview anchor should show the same dark bottle under the gripper; reject wrist geometry if it jumps to the bowl or cabinet.\n\nPlate: look for the white ceramic disc with red concentric rings. It can be confused with the gray stove burner because both are circular and flat in depth, so classify by RGB before using back_project. Sample the white inner region and ring-balanced pixels, not the rim alone; use the perceived center as a target, then bias a few cm deeper if the bottle hangs toward the near edge. Absolute coordinates from this run are counter-examples only and must not be cached.\n\n## Fragility flags\nThe most fragile step is the low release: a correct bottle grasp and a visually plausible placement may still not terminate if the bottle is on the plate rim/edge. Fallback is a short closed-gripper contact nudge at the same low z followed by a second release.\n\n## Difficulty and reliability\nConverged in 1 attempt with one in-episode recovery nudge. Expected single-shot rate is good when the grasp is visually confirmed and the release is followed by a low centering check. Residual risk: bottle hanging offset varies by grasp, so future runs should inspect the plate contact before deciding whether to nudge.\n\n## Cross-refs\n[[can-pick-visual-confirmation]]\n"

  "content": "---\nid: open-side-bowl-grasp\nscope: global\nkind: strategy\ntitle: Shift bowl grasps away from nearby fixture clutter.\napplies_when: A bowl target is crowded by a cabinet handle, rim, wall, or other fixture\n  on one side and Pi0 contacts without lifting.\nsymptom:\n- Pi0 contacts bowl but no lift\n- gripper reopens\n- crowded bowl grasp\n- handle blocks bowl\nevidence:\n  cells:\n  - spatial_swap_t3_s0\nconfidence: single-shot\nrelated: []\n---\n\n\nWhen a bowl is crowded by a fixture on one side, re-pre-position from the open side and use a plain visual prompt before increasing chunk budget.\n\n**Why:** the winning grasp followed two failed contact/no-lift attempts near the cabinet side; shifting toward the open table side let Pi0 close on the rim and lift.\n**How to apply:** after confirming the target identity in agentview, use wrist geometry to find the bowl, then offset the pre-position a few centimeters away from the obstruction. Use a short prompt such as `pick up the patterned bowl`, `max_chunks=14-18`, `lift_thresh=0.05`, and confirm gripper gap plus wrist evidence.\n**Falsify:** if the open-side approach still produces fully closed empty fingers or pushes the bowl off its support, the failure is not just fixture-side contact geometry.\n**Related:**\n"

  "size": 2053,
  "content": "---\nid: libero-in-predicate-fires-while-grasped\nscope: global\nkind: strategy\ntitle: Test placement targets by holding the object over them and watching libero_terminated,\n  before releasing\napplies_when: an In()/On() place task where the correct destination among several\n  look-alikes is uncertain, or where releasing risks tipping/losing the object\nsymptom:\n- wrong compartment\n- which container\n- ambiguous target\n- place predicate not firing\n- cannot re-grasp\n- tipped after release\n- in predicate\nevidence:\n  cells:\n  - 10_task_t5_s0\n  attempts: 4\n  solved_seeds:\n  - 0\nconfidence: single-shot\nrelated:\n- caddy-back-is-near-robot-pocket\n---\n\n\nLIBERO In()/On() success predicates check the OBJECT'S POSE, not the gripper\nstate, so `libero_terminated` flips the moment the held object's pose satisfies\nthe region \u2014 you do NOT have to release first.\n\n**Why:** libero_terminated mirrors the BDDL goal predicate, which is a function\nof object poses only. Releasing is irrelevant to the check (confirmed: placing a\nmug in the correct caddy pocket fired while still grasped; placing/releasing in\nthree WRONG pockets never fired).\n**How to apply:**\n- To disambiguate among candidate destinations, carry the still-grasped object\n  (gripper +1) low over each candidate and read `libero_terminated` from the\n  returned state. Move to the next candidate if it stays false \u2014 no release, no\n  re-grasp, no commitment. This turns an N-way target guess into N cheap probes.\n- Only `release` after the flag is already true (or to seat a confirmed target).\n- Corollary: a non-firing predicate with a clean, low, upright placement is\n  evidence of WRONG DESTINATION, not wrong physics \u2014 switch targets first.\n- Caveat: some tasks pair In() with a \"not in gripper\"/stack-stability term; if a\n  held probe won't fire but the geometry looks perfect, release once to check.\n**Falsify:** a place task where the predicate provably requires the gripper open\n(object released) and a correctly-posed held object does NOT fire.\n**Related:** [[caddy-back-is-near-robot-pocket]]\n"

Grasp each by handle/handle-root with a short max_chunks=8 call, firm, lift high, rotate the held payload about +90 degrees, remeasure its body offset, then carry through a +x corridor using move_pose at the retained yaw. Descend until plate-supported with the grip closed, then release. Yellow first was safe because the porcelain route stayed on the opposite side and used a high +x corridor.\n\nSuccess criteria: nonzero retained gap; wrist-confirmed airborne target; same-frame held-body center aligned to wrist-refined plate center; stable grip gap through descent; termination on final release.\n\n## Magic numbers\n\n- pi0 max_chunks=8 (usable band 7-10); reissue from a changed handle-side prepose rather than extending a rogue trajectory.\n- Firm grip 8-10 steps (usable band 8-12).\n- Carry z=0.70-0.72 m (usable band 0.68-0.75).\n- Held yaw rotation about +1.57 rad (usable band 1.35-1.60 after actual-yaw measurement).\n- move_pose step_clip=0.006-0.008 for carry; 0.003-0.004 for support descent.\n- Yellow support EEF z about 0.577 m at yaw 1.574; porcelain support stall about 0.565 m at yaw 1.370. Treat these as counter-examples, not cached coordinates.\n- NEVER carry with gripper=-1.\n- NEVER reuse a held offset from another pick.\n- NEVER infer plate center from a clipped agentview fragment; wrist-center it.\n\n## Failure modes\n\n| symptom | root cause (attempt) | fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| clean-looking placements under both signs remain false | edge-biased plate centers, wrong mapping, or release geometry were confounded across A6-A65 | use viewer mapping plus same-frame wrist body/plate alignment and final-release predicate |\n| inverted mug or large-yaw carry sweeps clutter | rotation/traverse performed before reaching a clear corridor (A66-A69) | rotate at high clear pose and carry via +x corridor |\n| distractor brace attempt tips target | Pi0 red acquisition drifted through yellow (A70-A71) | do not manipulate distractor; solve with offset redirection |\n| scripted plate pushes do nothing | top-down fingers pass above/interior of rim (A72) | leave plates fixed; wrist-localize true centers |\n| true-center egocentric configuration remains false | semantic assignment is wrong despite clean geometry (A73) | viewer-relative mapping |\n| yawed payload cannot reach plate center with move_to | held offset consumes the edge-axis reach | rotate offset into x and use move_pose |\n\n## Re-localization per scene\n\n- Yellow-white target: agentview semantic authority; bicolor yellow/white tapered mug with yellow handle. Prompt \u201cgrasp the yellow mug by the handle loop\u201d. Reject fully open fingers or cavity-only contact.\n- White target: textured porcelain-white mug, not the red patterned distractor. Prompt \u201cgrasp the white mug by the handle\u201d. A winning exterior/handle-root gap was about 32 mm before firming.\n- Plates: white ceramic discs with concentric red rings. Use wrist view over each plate and back-project its visible center; agentview edge fragments underestimate the outer plate center by several centimeters.\n- Absolute coordinates from this seed must not be cached. Counter-example only: plate centers were near y=-0.292 and +0.319.\n\n## Fragility flags\n\nMost fragile is the far +y porcelain delivery. If natural hang demands EEF y beyond reach, rotate the held mug about +90 degrees at high z, measure the new offset, then move_pose at the actual yaw. Recenter after every rotation drift.\n\n## Difficulty and reliability\n\nSolved on the 69th archived attempt across multiple agents. Expected single-shot reliability is low until both semantics and per-pick offsets are handled; once the winning viewer mapping, handle grasps, +90-degree offset redirection, and wrist plate centers are used together, the final predicate fired during release.\n\n## Cross-refs\n\n[[held-offset-rotation-reach]]\n[[rotate-wrist-90deg-drifts-eef-recenter-after]]\n[[pi0-grasp-tall-mug-by-handle]]\n[[place-order-never-carry-over-placed-object]]\n"

  "content": "---\nid: post-grasp-yaw-offset\nscope: global\nkind: strategy\ntitle: Rotate a held bowl after a reliable grasp to move its offset into reach\napplies_when: A reliable Pi0 bowl grasp carries the object with a large offset that\n  makes direct placement miss or hit the workspace edge\nsymptom:\n- held offset\n- workspace edge\n- bowl beside plate\n- gripper center wrong\n- placement misses\nevidence:\n  cells:\n  - spatial_swap_t9_s0\n  attempts: 6\nconfidence: single-shot\nrelated:\n- visual-over-pick-heuristic\n---\n\n\nWhen the grasp is reliable but the carried bowl offset points toward an unreachable placement correction, preserve the grasp and rotate the wrist after the lift so the object offset can be compensated along a reachable axis.\n\n**Why:** Pi0's cabinet-rim grasp held the bowl with a large offset from the EEF. Direct compensation in the original orientation repeatedly required more negative x than the OSC workspace allowed. A post-grasp yaw rotation of about +1.57 rad changed the visible bowl-to-gripper relationship while keeping the grasp, allowing a short reachable descent where the bowl body overlapped the plate.\n**How to apply:** First get a visually confirmed grasp with the original successful prompt and pose. Hold `gripper=+1`, apply `rotate_wrist` after the lift (`delta_yaw` roughly +/-1.57; choose sign by wrist view), then carry slowly with `step_clip=0.008-0.015`. Before release, use wrist RGB to verify the object body, not EEF center, overlaps the target surface.\n**Falsify:** If rotating after the grasp consistently drops the object or leaves the bowl-to-gripper offset unchanged in wrist view, this strategy is not the right lever for that grasp.\n**Related:** [[visual-over-pick-heuristic]]\n"
}

Pi0 pi0_pick failed twice (closed to 2 mm = air, because Pi0 aimed 13 mm off the bowl centre x). Recovered by scripting the grasp myself: a closed-gripper probe descended onto the rim and stalled at z=0.9438, which located both the rim height and the correct y on the rim wall (also proved the fingertip bottom equals the EEF z). Pinching the flared lip slipped twice; pinching the wall just below the lip at eef (-0.116, 0.045, 0.929) held. Pick verified without an oracle via a z-banded region back-projection (no bowl points left at table height). Carried with the measured rigid offset bowl-centre = eef + (0,-0.031) in two hops to the re-localized plate centre (0.0555,-0.0376,0.9087) and released; On() fired immediately. Notably discarded the wrist world map after a landmark cross-check showed a 3.6 cm xy bias (Z was fine). Audit and recipe written to the specified artifact paths."
}
